 LA advances effort to crack down on illegal dumping

 By City News Service | news@socalnews.com PUBLISHED: November 18, 2026 at 1:58 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The Los Angeles City Council on Wednesday laid the groundwork to bolster illegal dumping enforcement by potentially increasing fines and allocating additional resources to the issue.
 In a 12-0 vote, the council instructed the Bureau of Sanitation, Los Angeles Police Department, city attorney and other relevant departments to report within 30 days on illegal dumping enforcement activities and the status of funding allocated in the 2026-27 budget. The report is expected to outline recommendations on needed resources and funding for strengthening the city’s response to the problem.
 Additionally, the council called on the Bureau of Sanitation to explore using existing contracts, technology and equipment being used by other city teams for identifying, documenting, investigating and prosecuting illegal dumping activity.
 The council further asked staff to develop a citywide inventory of chronic illegal dumping hot spots in each council district. City attorneys will work on providing options to update penalties for illegal dumping, as well as increasing rewards for successful prosecutions, and align fees with other municipalities throughout the state.
 There was no discussion on the matter. Council members Nithya Raman, Curren Price and Monica Rodriguez were absent during the vote.
 In September, Councilwoman Imelda Padilla introduced a motion to address illegal dumping. She described the issue as negatively impacting taxpayers, public health, public safety, environmental quality and communities.
 “While the city has made investments in identifying and removing illegally dumped waste, illegal dumping must be addressed as a comprehensive three pronged strategy, consisting of cleanup and abatement, education and prevention, and investigation and enforcement with meaningful penalties,” the motion stated.
 Padilla said the city needs to increase fines for them to have an impact. Under the current fine structure, illegal dumping results in a $500 fine for a first violation, $750 fine for a second violation, and $1,000 for third and subsequent violations.
 Other jurisdictions such as Santa Cruz County impose penalties of $2,500 for a first illegal dumping violation, followed by $5,000 for a second violation within one year, and $10,000 for a third or subsequent violation within one year.
 “However, fines alone will not solve the city’s illegal dumping problem,” the motion added. “Effective enforcement requires investigators, technology, data, cleanup capacity, coordination and sustained attention to the locations where dumping repeatedly occurs.”
